additional_info.body:
Hallo Benjamin, good morning. I hope all is well.
Thank you for the feedback.
Here is what I can see from the router for charger iwuJDH:
As you can see it mentions that the WAN port is not being used and has a
Red Cross.
There are some possible root causes on why this connection is not working:
Ethernet cable is not inserted properly
Ethernet cable is damaged/faulty
Missing connection from FA6 to Router2 (there should be a green wire to the WAN port)
FA6 is faulty and not transmitting to the WAN port of Router2
If this is the case we can try redirecting the Ethernet cable directly to the WAN port of Router2 and check again.
Worst case scenario: the Router2's WAN port is faulty and needs to be replaced.
In the other charger you have provided to me, it doesn't have the same version so the UI is different, it doesn't have the same information as the first photo but I can see that there was an exchange of data of 5.38Mb so at some point this charger was connected.
Let me know if you are able to troubleshoot this yourself and provide me feedback or if I should arrange a regional Siemens technician to support this activity.
I will wait for your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0404139-DC/SI-D/DE[iwuJDH] - OCPP offline CRM:00315002323
additional_info.body:
Hi Benjamin,
I believe there is some misunderstanding, the Modbus TCP connection is different from OCPP connection.
The difference between both is the following:
OCPP connection is just a regular internet connection that you have to a backend where you can do several things like allow certain vehicles/RFID cards and monitor the activity of the charger.
Modbus is a communication protocol that is primarily used for industrial automation and control systems. It is designed for communication between devices on a local network, such as between a programmable logic controller (PLC) and various field devices.
This is usually used for the ELMS (external load management system) where you can change certain available parameters or monitor said parameters via PLC or similar.
In this case, there is no need to have a OCPP connection, it is only required an Ethernet cable in XF3 (Router1) WAN port or FA13.
Here is where we usually use these certains configurations that you mentioned:
192.168.1.200 and the port 400.
I will wait for your feedback before proceding with the changes.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
